10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates zero-shot classification using text descriptions alone, already covered in this topic, with no labeled training examples.

code.content:
import math

def cosine_similarity(a, b):
    # already covered generally as cosine similarity in Sentence Embeddings
    dot = sum(x * y for x, y in zip(a, b))
    norm_a = math.sqrt(sum(x * x for x in a))
    norm_b = math.sqrt(sum(y * y for y in b))
    return dot / (norm_a * norm_b)

# already covered as a joint embedding space in Vision Language Models
image_embedding = [0.15, 0.85, 0.3]  # an unlabeled image, never seen during training

# already covered as describing classes with text instead in this topic
class_descriptions = {
    "a photo of a bicycle": [0.2, 0.8, 0.25],
    "a photo of a mountain": [0.1, 0.2, 0.9],
    "a photo of a bird": [0.6, 0.5, 0.1],
}

print("Zero-shot classification, using genuinely only text descriptions (already covered in this topic):\n")
scores = {}
for description, description_embedding in class_descriptions.items():
    similarity = cosine_similarity(image_embedding, description_embedding)
    scores[description] = similarity
    print(f"  '{description}': {similarity:.3f}")

predicted_class = max(scores, key=scores.get)
print(f"\nPredicted class (already covered in this topic): '{predicted_class}'")
print("Genuinely no labeled training examples of any of these classes were ever used")

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: Zero-shot learning recognizes a class the model has never seen a single training example of.
It removes even the small remaining example requirement that few-shot learning still needed.
A new class gets described using plain text, which substitutes entirely for labeled examples.
CLIP already demonstrated this capability, comparing an image against candidate text descriptions.
Zero-shot recognition only works because text and images already share one common embedding space.
Language models perform a closely related zero-shot behavior through prompting, with no examples given.
With zero examples to learn from, zero-shot accuracy tends to trail few-shot accuracy.
Zero-shot learning suits brand new classes with no labels; few-shot suits classes with a few examples.
